entities.text: Paletinarayana Reddy, vs State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Honourable Sri Justice D.V.S.S. Somayajulu
 Criminal Petition No.3695 of 2019
Order:
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
This Criminal Petition is filed to quash all further proceedings in C.C.No.23 of 2019 on the file of the VI Metropolitan Magistrate at Vijayawada.
The case of the petitioner is that the charge sheet that has been filed is not maintainable as the same is filed under section 7 read with 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

The foremost submission is that the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been repealed and the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 (in short "the FSS Act-2006") has come into force from 05.08.2011.
Therefore, he questions the very filing of the charge sheet itself.
In addition, learned counsel also submits that the petitioner before this Court is the owner of the premises and that he has leased the said premises to the company in August, 2015 to accused No.2.
Therefore, he submits that in view of the rental deeds, which are entered into, he is not responsible for the business and accused No.2 alone can be prosecuted.
He prays for quashing of the proceedings.
In reply to this, learned Public Prosecutor submits that quashing of the entire proceedings is not called for.
He submits that the other sections of IPC also applicable. even if the FSS Act-2006 applies.
He also submits that petitioner-Accused No.1 is actively involved in the business and that the lease deeds are created for the purpose of this case.
He says both Accused No.1 and Accused No.2 are involved and they should be prosecuted.
This Court after hearing both the learned counsel notices that the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, 2011 has come into force with effect from 05.08.2011.
Therefore, the filing of the charge sheet under Section 7 and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is legally untenable.
The case started with a raid conducted on the premises in January, 2017.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that charging the petitioner for an offence under a repealed Act is incorrect.
The proceedings under Sections 420 and 272 of IPC can however proceed.
Whether the lease deeds executed between accused Nos.1 and 2 are validly executed or not is the matter to be decided in the trial Court.
Hence, on the ground that the lease was granted to accused No.2, the petitioner-accused No.1 cannot claim complete exoneration from the case.
Therefore, the Criminal Petition is allowed in part.
The charge sheet, in so far as it relates to Sections 7 and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is set aside.
The proceedings under Sections 420 and 272 of IPC shall go on.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Criminal Petition shall stand closed.

D.V.S.S. SOMAYAJULU, J Date:16.08.2019 Ssv Paletinarayana Reddy, vs State Of Ap on 16 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197505654/
